title: EU AML Regulation (AMLR) for non-bank lenders | Customer Due Diligence Guide
summary: Non-bank lenders are obliged entities under the EU AMLR from 10 July 2027: when CDD applies, what AMLA's draft standards change and how to prepare.
body_markdown:
*What the EU AMLR and AMLA's final draft standards mean for online loan applications, occasional transactions and remote identification.*


Undertakings that carry out lending without being credit institutions, including consumer credit providers, are financial institutions and therefore obliged entities under the EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation (AMLR), which applies directly from 10 July 2027. A lender must apply customer due diligence when it establishes a business relationship and when it carries out an occasional transaction of EUR 10,000 or more, in a single operation or through linked transactions. Under AMLA's final draft standards, remote verification is expected to use suitable eIDs, including the EU Digital Identity Wallet (EUDI Wallet), or relevant qualified trust services wherever possible.


*Written by Aleksander Wasiak (Compliance Officer) and Patryk Pietrzak (Head of Growth), Authologic.*
